description: Dimensionless imaginary part of the complex linear gyrokinetic eigenmode frequency, divided by the positive reference angular frequency, at a specified wavevector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field in the local flux-tube approximation. Positive values represent exponential growth and negative values represent damping.
documentation:
Dimensionless imaginary part of the complex linear gyrokinetic eigenmode frequency, divided by the positive reference angular frequency, is the normalized temporal growth rate of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode at a specified wavevector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field in the local flux-tube approximation. It identifies the exponential amplitude change of that eigenmode in linear gyrokinetic theory.

The defining normalization is

$$
\gamma_\mathrm{norm} = \frac{\operatorname{Im}\omega}{\omega_\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\omega$ is the complex eigenfrequency for time dependence $\exp(-i\omega t)$ and $\omega_\mathrm{ref}>0$ is the reference angular frequency used for the normalized eigenfrequency. When the reference angular frequency is written as $v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}/L_\mathrm{ref}$, this is equivalently $\gamma_\mathrm{norm}=\gamma L_\mathrm{ref}/v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}$, with $\gamma=\operatorname{Im}\omega$, $v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}$ the reference thermal speed, and $L_\mathrm{ref}$ the reference length scale.

This quantity is for one linear gyrokinetic eigenmode at one specified perpendicular wavevector, not for a spectrum-averaged rate, nonlinear turbulent growth, or finite-amplitude envelope evolution. It is the imaginary-part counterpart to the [normalized_frequency_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode](name:frequency_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), which uses the real part of the same $\omega$; the eigenmode-specific scope distinguishes it from [normalized_growth_rate](name:linear_growth_rate_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), which does not by itself require a linear gyrokinetic eigenvalue.

Sign convention: Positive when the eigenmode amplitude increases exponentially with time.

dd_sources.documentation: Growth rate

label_note: links its own name as a different, more general 'normalized_growth_rate'; otherwise Im(omega)/omega_ref as the source

description: Fusion-neutron number flux incident on the neutron detector’s active surface, giving the rate at which neutrons cross each unit of that surface.
documentation:
This quantity is the incident fusion-neutron number flux on the neutron-sensitive active surface of the detector. It is the surface-crossing flux, not the neutron production rate or the registered detection-event rate described by [rate of neutron detector]. The parent quantity [flux of neutron detector] expresses the same surface-transport concept.

The defining relation is

$$
\Phi_n = \frac{dN_n}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Phi_n$ is the incident neutron number flux, $N_n$ is the number of neutrons crossing the active surface, $A$ is active surface area, and $t$ is time. The surface is the neutron-sensitive area characterized by [area of neutron detector]; passive housing, shielding, supports, and electronics are excluded. Registered event rates additionally depend on detector response and efficiency.

dd_sources.documentation: Neutron flux impinging on the detector, deduced from the measured count-rate (relevant only when mode/identifier/index = 1)

label_note: writes Phi_n where the registry flux symbol is Gamma; unresolved [rate of neutron detector], [flux of neutron detector] and [area of neutron detector]

description: Global particle-number throughput removed from the plasma by pumping at the wall, independent of any particular carrier species and distinct from an areal flux.
documentation:
The wall-attributed pumping rate is the global particle-number throughput removed from the plasma through the wall by a pumping process. It applies to the aggregate removed particle population without selecting a particular species or charge state.

The rate is defined as

$$
R_{\rm pump} = \frac{dN_{\rm removed}}{dt}
$$

where $R_{\rm pump}$ is the pumping-related particle-removal rate, $N_{\rm removed}$ is the cumulative number of particles removed through the wall, and $t$ is time.

This quantity is a global throughput rather than a local particle flux per unit wall area; spatially resolved wall fluxes must be integrated over the relevant wall surface before forming this rate. It excludes particle removal mechanisms not attributed to pumping. The quantity is the wall-localized specialization of [rate due to pumping](name:rate_due_to_pumping), while [particle rate at wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping) makes the particle-channel interpretation explicit without restricting the carrier species.
label_note: writes R_pump where the registry rate symbol is dot-N

description: Signed plasma-induced change in the effective optical path accumulated along an interferometer beam relative to its corresponding no-plasma reference path.
documentation:
This quantity is the signed plasma-induced change in effective optical path length accumulated along an electromagnetic propagation path represented by an interferometer beam. It describes an optical delay or advance caused by the plasma, rather than the unperturbed geometric path length.

The variation is defined as

$$
\Delta L = L_{\mathrm{plasma}} - L_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\Delta L$ is the optical path-length variation, $L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the effective optical path along the beam in the presence of plasma, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the corresponding effective path without plasma.

This quantity applies to the net change accumulated along the interferometer beam's complete line of sight. It is a path-integrated optical quantity, not a local path-length density, an unperturbed geometric length, or a separate phase-calibration coefficient. As the variation of [length of an interferometer beam](name:length_of_interferometer_beam), it expresses the plasma-induced departure from the reference path. The associated phase shift provides the optical information used to derive [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the plasma-affected effective optical path length exceeds the corresponding no-plasma reference path.

description: Effective Fickian coefficient relating the diffusive flux of total momentum to its local momentum-density gradient without selecting a directional component.
documentation:
Total momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the diffusive flux of aggregated momentum and the negative local gradient of aggregated momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for momentum transport.

For each resolved transport direction, the componentwise closure is

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}\left(\sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,i}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of total momentum component $i$, $D_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the corresponding total momentum diffusivity component, $x_i$ is the spatial coordinate in direction $i$, $s$ indexes the momentum-carrying populations included in the total, $m_s$ is the particle mass of population $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, and $v_{s,i}$ is its velocity component in direction $i$.

The total aggregation sums the momentum contributions of all populations and charge states included in the physical definition rather than selecting one species, charge state, or process. The quantity remains direction-general and vector-valued; no single toroidal, radial, parallel, or other projection is selected at this level.

This quantity is the total-momentum specialization of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), retaining its Fick's-law transport meaning while fixing the population aggregation. The [toroidal total momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_total_momentum_diffusivity) is the directional specialization obtained by selecting the toroidal component of this vector.
label_note: Fick closure on the summed momentum density in m^2/s; no registry entry applies; links resolve

description: Instantaneous ammonia source rate expressed as equivalent-electron count per time, assigning ten count units to each neutral NH3 molecule introduced into the plasma vessel.
documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate of ammonia delivery to the plasma vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention for neutral ammonia molecules. It represents injected NH3 inventory, not the plasma electron source or the ionization state of ammonia.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 10\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the molecular ammonia injection rate, and the factor 10 is the total atomic-electron count of one neutral NH3 molecule. Time integration gives the corresponding [accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count). The isotopologue-specific counterpart is [ammonia_deuterated_source_rate](name:ammonia_deuterated_source_rate).

description: Radial (R-direction) component of the total electric current-density vector at a plasma-facing wall in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height. It is signed positive toward increasing R.
documentation:
Radial (R-direction) component of the total electric current-density vector at a plasma-facing wall is the projection of the local total electric current-density vector onto the $\hat{R}$ basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining projection at a wall point $\mathbf{x}_w$ is:

$$
j_{R,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{wall}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}_w) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $j_{R,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{wall}}$ denotes this scalar quantity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total [current_density](name:current_density), $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the local unit vector toward increasing $R$, and $\mathbf{x}_w$ lies on the plasma-facing material wall.

Total means all current-carrying contributions included in the physical current-density vector, such as inductive, neoclassical, wave-driven, kinetic, conductive, charged-particle, and sheath-mediated currents. This quantity is the wall-evaluated radial projection of the total vector, not a process-resolved contribution such as [radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). A tile current such as [current_of_divertor_tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile) is a surface integral of the current-density component normal to that tile; it equals an area integral of this radial component only where the tile normal is parallel to $\hat{R}$.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ at the wall points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

description: Maximum allowed value of the signed rotation angle of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror within its mechanical travel range.
documentation:
The upper mechanical travel limit is the greatest permitted value of the mirror’s signed rotation angle, bounding the accessible steering range of the launcher. It is a limit of the mechanical actuator, not the mirror angle during a particular operating condition.

Let $\theta$ denote the signed mirror angle defined by [angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror]. The upper limit $\theta_{\max}$ is defined by

$$
\theta_{\max} = \sup\{\theta \mid \theta\text{ is mechanically accessible}\}
$$

The quantity excludes the lower travel limit and does not describe the mirror’s position unless that position equals the upper boundary of the allowed range.

Sign convention: Positive when the mirror rotates in the positive sense defined for [angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror].

description: Stiff coefficient multiplying ion temperature to form the implicit contribution to the ion energy source term.
documentation:
This quantity is the stiff implicit linear coefficient of the energy source or sink for the applicable ion population. It represents the temperature-dependent part of the ion energy source that is treated implicitly during time integration.

The implicit ion energy-source contribution is defined by

$$
S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} = \alpha_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} T_i
$$

where $S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit ion energy source contribution, $\alpha_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this source-rate coefficient, $T_i$ is the local ion temperature, and the superscript $\mathrm{imp}$ denotes the implicit contribution. The subscript $E$ identifies the energy channel and $i$ identifies the applicable ion population.

The coefficient applies to the ion-species member represented by the ion channel; it is not summed over all ion species, does not represent a total-ion quantity, and does not select a particular ion charge state. It belongs to the energy channel and is distinct from particle- and momentum-source coefficients. The explicit, non-stiff remainder of the ion energy source is excluded. For positive ion temperature, a positive coefficient produces an energy gain and a negative coefficient produces an energy loss.

Its role is analogous to the electron-channel coefficient [implicit electron energy-source rate coefficient](name:implicit_electron_energy_source_rate), while [total implicit ion particle-source rate coefficient](name:total_implicit_ion_particle_source_rate) differs in both transport channel and ion aggregation.

dd_sources.documentation: Implicit part of the source term, i.e. to be multiplied by the equation's primary quantity

label_note: defines the coefficient as S/T_i, which carries m^-3 s^-1 per unit energy rather than the unit s^-1; the source multiplies the equation's primary quantity, not T_i alone; also misses the source-rate opening and writes alpha where the registry symbol is S

description: Repeat arclength along the sensing-fiber centerline at which the effective birefringent-axis orientation completes one spatial cycle.
documentation:
The twist period is the repeat arclength along the sensing-fiber centerline for the effective birefringent-axis orientation to return to the same state.

Let $s$ denote arclength along the fiber centerline and $Q(s)$ denote the specified effective birefringent-axis state. The twist period $L_{\rm tw}$ is defined by

$$
Q(s + L_{\rm tw}) = Q(s)
$$

where $L_{\rm tw}$ is the smallest positive repeat arclength.

This is the twist-specific member of the [fiber optic current sensor period]. It describes spatial repetition of the optical anisotropy, not the total fiber arclength, the [initial twist phase](name:initial_spun_twist_phase_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor), or the [polarization beat length].

dd_sources.documentation: Twist period

label_note: unresolved [fiber optic current sensor period] and [polarization beat length]

description: Cumulative energy transferred from a plasma-facing component into its coolant over the pulse, excluding energy retained in the component or transferred elsewhere.
documentation:
The quantity is the energy cumulatively absorbed by active coolant from a specified plasma-facing component during the accumulation interval. It represents thermal energy removed from that component, not an instantaneous transfer rate or the component's total deposited energy.

$$
E_{\mathrm{cool}}(t) = \int_{t_0}^{t} P_{\mathrm{cool}}(\tau)\,d\tau
$$

Here, $E_{\mathrm{cool}}(t)$ is the accumulated coolant-absorbed energy at evaluation time $t$; $t_0$ is the pulse start and lower limit of accumulation; $P_{\mathrm{cool}}(\tau)$ is the instantaneous thermal power extracted by the coolant from the component at integration time $\tau$. The power corresponds to the wall coolant-removal concept described by [total thermal coolant-absorbed power at the wall](name:total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall).

The scope is one specified plasma-facing component and its active coolant, with contributions accumulated from pulse start to the evaluation time. Only energy transferred into that coolant is included; energy retained in the component, radiated away, carried by particles, or transferred to unrelated coolant circuits is excluded.

The accumulated energy is the time integral of the corresponding coolant-absorbed power, so its time derivative equals $P_{\mathrm{cool}}(t)$ when the accumulation is continuous. It is therefore distinct from the instantaneous power quantity and from deposited energy that has not necessarily been removed by coolant.
label_note: time integral of the coolant-extracted power from pulse start; no registry entry applies; link resolves

description: Y-axis component of the unit vector along the first measurement axis of a structural strain-rosette gage, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
documentation:
Y-axis component of the unit vector along the first measurement axis of a structural strain-rosette gage is the scalar projection of that oriented measurement-axis unit vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$. It is a direction cosine describing gage orientation, not a strain value.

The component is defined by the dot product:

$$
u_{1y} = \mathbf{u}_1 \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $u_{1y}$ is this y-axis component, $\mathbf{u}_1$ is the unit vector along the first measurement axis of the structural strain-rosette gage, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

Together with the corresponding [x-axis component] and [z-axis component], it specifies the full orientation of the first measurement axis and satisfies the unit-vector normalization $u_{1x}^2 + u_{1y}^2 + u_{1z}^2 = 1$. It is distinct from the [y-axis component of the unit vector along the second measurement axis].

Sign convention: Positive when the unit vector along the first measurement axis of the structural strain-rosette gage has a component in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

dd_sources.documentation: Component along Y axis

label_note: unresolved [x-axis component], [z-axis component] and [y-axis component of the unit vector along the second measurement axis]

description: Volume-integrated explicit torque vector acting on the combined ion population, summed over ion species and charge states and independent of the primary transported momentum variable.
documentation:
This quantity is the global explicit source or sink of angular momentum for the combined ion population, represented as a torque vector integrated over the relevant plasma volume. It retains the full directional torque rather than selecting a single cylindrical component.

The volume-integrated torque is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{T}_{i,\mathrm{exp}} = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}$ is the explicit ion torque vector, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}$ is the corresponding local torque-density vector, $V$ is the relevant plasma volume, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is its volume element. The subscript $i$ denotes the combined ion population, and $\mathrm{exp}$ denotes the explicit source contribution.

The quantity applies globally to all included ion species and ionic charge states, which are summed rather than represented separately. It is independent of the primary transported momentum variable and excludes any torque contribution defined solely through that variable; it is also distinct from a local torque density and from a single-direction projection.

The broader [ion torque](name:ion_torque) is the net volume-integrated torque on the ion population, while [toroidal explicit ion torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque) is the toroidal projection of this explicit vector contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when each vector component points in its corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
label_note: volume integral of the explicit ion torque density, summed over ion states; i as the registry gives; links resolve

description: Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the y direction cosine, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) basis, of the unit vector from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center.
documentation:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the signed projection, in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, of the unit vector directed from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center. It is the y direction cosine of that line-of-sight direction.

The component is defined by projecting the detector-directed unit vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis vector:

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}} \cdot \hat{y} = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}) \cdot \hat{y}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}} \rVert}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the unit vector from the field-of-view voxel center to the detector center, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector-center position, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}$ is the field-of-view voxel-center position, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity is a signed direction-cosine component, not a position coordinate, distance, or unnormalized displacement component. Together with the corresponding x and z components it satisfies $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ when the field-of-view voxel center and detector center are distinct.

dd_sources.documentation: Component along Y axis  for each voxel

description: Calibration polarization angle of an optical element is the signed angle from a reference transverse polarization direction to the element's selected polarization axis, viewed along its line of sight toward the plasma.
documentation:
Calibration polarization angle of an optical element is the orientation angle of the polarization-selective axis of that element in the plane perpendicular to its line of sight. It identifies the electric-field component selected by the element relative to a defined transverse reference direction.

The signed angle is defined by

$$
\alpha_\mathrm{cal} = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-\hat{\ell}\cdot\left(\hat{e}_\mathrm{ref}\times\hat{e}_\mathrm{sel}\right),\ \hat{e}_\mathrm{ref}\cdot\hat{e}_\mathrm{sel}\right]
$$

where $\hat{\ell}$ is the line-of-sight unit vector directed from the optical element toward the plasma, $\hat{e}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference polarization unit vector in the plane normal to $\hat{\ell}$, and $\hat{e}_\mathrm{sel}$ is the selected polarization-axis unit vector in the same transverse plane.

This quantity is an axis-alignment calibration parameter, not a measure of polarization ellipticity, polarization purity, or the handedness of a full polarization state.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected polarization axis is rotated counter-clockwise from the reference transverse polarization direction as seen looking from the optical element toward the plasma along the line of sight.

description: Full physical extent of a hard X-ray detector aperture along the detector's second local tangential direction, for rectangular aperture geometry.
documentation:
Full physical extent of a hard X-ray detector aperture along the detector's second local tangential direction is the edge-to-edge size of the active opening in that object-local tangential direction. It applies to rectangular aperture geometry, where the aperture has separate first and second local tangential full extents in its plane.

This quantity applies only to the detector aperture and only to the second local tangential extent of that aperture. It is not a signed coordinate, not a detector position, not a detector thickness along the local normal, and not the first local tangential extent represented by the [width of the hard-X-ray detector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector).

For a rectangular detector aperture, this height and the [detector width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector) define the aperture's two in-plane dimensions and are geometric inputs to the [hard-X-ray detector etendue](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector). The analogous second local tangential full extent of the filter-window aperture is the [height of the hard-X-ray filter window], which refers to a different optical element.

description: Length of the major oblique side of a plasma-filament cross-section, inclined relative to the major-radius axis and distinct from the height-oriented side.
documentation:
Major length of a plasma filament is the Euclidean length of the oblique parallelogram side associated with the major-radius direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the side lies in the poloidal $R$-$Z$ cross-section and is defined by

$$
L_{\mathrm{major}} = \sqrt{(\Delta R)^2 + (\Delta Z)^2}
$$

where $L_{\mathrm{major}}$ is the major oblique-side length, $\Delta R$ is the difference in major-radius coordinates between the side endpoints, and $\Delta Z$ is the corresponding difference in vertical coordinates.

This quantity applies to one discrete plasma current-carrying filament element and describes only its major oblique side. It is an individual geometric length, not a sum, average, or aggregate over filament elements, and it excludes the other oblique side represented by the [minor length of a plasma filament](name:minor_length_of_plasma_filament).

It is the major-qualified component of [length of a plasma filament], selecting the side associated with the major-radius direction rather than defining an additional length to be added to the parent quantity. Its inclination is described separately by the [inclination angle of a plasma filament](name:alpha_angle_of_plasma_filament).

description: Vertical (Z) coordinate locating the geometric center of an annulus in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
documentation:
The quantity is the vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an annular cross section. It locates the annulus along the vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

For annulus-center position $\mathbf{r}_c$, the coordinate is defined by

$$
z_c = Z(\mathbf{r}_c)
$$

where $z_c$ is the vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the geometric-center position of the annulus, and $Z(\mathbf{r}_c)$ is the vertical coordinate function evaluated at that position.

The quantity applies to annular component cross sections, including those associated with coils, loops, ferritic objects, and iron-core segments. It describes the center point only; it is not the vertical coordinate of the annulus boundary, an average over the annular area, or a plasma-field quantity.

It is the annular-geometry counterpart of the [vertical coordinate of a rectangle center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rectangle_center): both identify the vertical coordinate of a cross-sectional geometric center, while this quantity applies specifically to an annulus.

description: Fast electron power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
documentation:
Fast electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power transferred to the fast, non-thermal electron population throughout the plasma volume. It is the fast-electron component of [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power).

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron absorbed wave power, $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local coherent-wave power density absorbed by fast electrons at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity excludes wave power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons, ions, and other populations, as well as wave power that is launched but not absorbed. Unlike [fast electron power at inside flux surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it represents the total plasma-volume integral rather than a cumulative value inside a specified flux surface. The population scope is complementary to [thermal electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

description: Major-radius component of a shattered-pellet fragment velocity, resolved along the R direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
documentation:
This quantity is the signed major-radius component of the velocity of an individual shattered-pellet fragment. It describes fragment motion along the cylindrical direction associated with increasing major radius.

The component is defined by

$$
v_R = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{frag}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $v_R$ is the major-radius velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{frag}}$ is the fragment velocity vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing major radius. The right-handed cylindrical frame $(R, \phi, Z)$ uses $R$ for major radius, $\phi$ for toroidal angle, and $Z$ for vertical height.

The quantity applies to a shattered-pellet fragment rather than to the center-of-mass velocity of the entire fragment cloud, and it represents one directional component rather than the fragment-speed magnitude. Together with the [toroidal velocity of the pellet](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet) and [vertical velocity of the pellet](name:vertical_velocity_of_pellet), it provides directional components of shattered-pellet motion.

Sign convention: Positive when the fragment moves toward increasing major radius $R$.

Major radius component of the velocity of the centre of mass of the pellet

description: Net conventional electric current carried by charged particles into all divertor target surfaces, including signed electron and ion contributions.
documentation:
The total divertor current is the algebraic conventional current delivered by charged particles crossing the plasma-facing surfaces of the complete divertor assembly. It includes ion and electron contributions and excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current.

The current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the total current in A, $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of divertor target surfaces, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is conventional charged-particle current density in A m$^{-2}$, $q_s$ is the signed charge of species $s$ in C, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is its particle flux density in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ points from the plasma toward the material.

This assembly-integrated quantity differs from [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target), which applies to one target, and [current of a divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile), which applies to an individual tile.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional charged-particle current flows from the plasma into the divertor material.

description: Euclidean length of the alpha-side of a ferritic element’s oblique parallelogram cross-section, measured in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
documentation:
The quantity is the non-negative Euclidean length of the alpha-side, the designated inclined edge of a ferritic element’s oblique parallelogram cross-section. It is the alpha-side-specific component of [length of a ferritic element], rather than the length of an unspecified cross-sectional edge.

For endpoints $(R_1,Z_1)$ and $(R_2,Z_2)$ of the alpha-side in the poloidal plane,

$$
L_\alpha = \sqrt{(R_2-R_1)^2+(Z_2-Z_1)^2}
$$

where $R_i$ are major-radius coordinates and $Z_i$ are vertical coordinates, both in meters, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The toroidal coordinate is fixed for this poloidal cross-sectional length. The quantity is a magnitude and is therefore non-negative.

dd_sources.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle alpha with respect to the major radius axis

label_note: opens 'The quantity is' against 'Length {locus}'; unresolved [length of a ferritic element]

description: Signed z-axis direction cosine of a strain gage’s second measurement-direction unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
documentation:
The second measurement-direction unit vector of a strain gage specifies the orientation of its second sensing axis. Its z-axis direction cosine is the signed projection of that orientation onto the Cartesian z axis.

$$
d_{2z} = \hat{\mathbf{d}}_2 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $d_{2z}$ is the z-axis direction cosine, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_2$ is the unit vector along the second measurement direction, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector of the z axis in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame. For a unit direction vector, $-1 \leq d_{2z} \leq 1$. The second-direction component complements the [z-axis direction cosine of the first measurement direction] and is distinct from the [z coordinate of the sensor attachment point](name:z_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point), which specifies location rather than orientation.

Sign convention: Positive when the second measurement direction has a component toward increasing $z$.

dd_sources.documentation: Component along Z axis

label_note: unresolved [z-axis direction cosine of the first measurement direction]

description: Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma. It describes the beam's post-propagation transverse polarization state, not the incident state or the ellipse orientation.
documentation:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma is the ellipticity of that beam. It characterizes the relative electric-field semiamplitudes of the post-propagation transverse polarization ellipse.

The ellipticity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{b}{a}
$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the polarization ellipticity, $a$ is the major-axis semiamplitude of the electric-field polarization ellipse, and $b$ is the signed minor-axis semiamplitude of that ellipse. The magnitude satisfies $|\varepsilon| \leq 1$.

This quantity applies to the polarimeter beam after it has traversed the magnetized plasma and is therefore distinct from the [initial polarization ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam). It is a polarization-shape parameter and excludes the orientation of the ellipse; rotation of that orientation is represented by the [Faraday angle](name:faraday_angle). The quantity refers to a single beam polarization state, with no aggregation over distinct beam paths.

Magnetized-plasma birefringence can transform the [initial polarization ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam) into this post-propagation ellipticity by changing the polarization ellipse during propagation; that change is distinct from Faraday rotation of the ellipse orientation.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field vector rotates in a right-handed sense about the beam-propagation direction.

dd_sources.documentation: Ellipticity

label_note: writes epsilon where the registry ellipticity symbol is e (which collides with the electron subscript, so the registry entry is the harder fault)

description: Temporal frequency associated with a wave-diagnostic channel, defining the oscillation or probing frequency used to establish its plasma interaction.
documentation:
The wave-diagnostic-channel frequency is the temporal rate of oscillation of the electromagnetic wave associated with a channel. It specifies the frequency at which the channel interacts with or samples the plasma.

The relation between temporal frequency $f$ and angular frequency $\omega$ is

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is the temporal frequency, $\omega$ is the angular frequency of the wave, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

This quantity applies to one wave-diagnostic channel and is not a sum or average over channels, frequency values, or wave power. For a frequency-swept probing channel, each selected frequency defines the probing state used to determine the corresponding plasma response or cutoff location; for a resonance channel, it identifies the wave frequency associated with the probed resonance.

The channel-owned quantity is distinct from the broader [wave frequency](name:wave_frequency) concept and from the beam-owned [frequency of an electron-cyclotron beam](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam). It describes frequency, not the duration of a sweep or the electromagnetic energy-transfer rate represented by [wave power](name:wave_power).

dd_sources.documentation: Frequency of the channel
Array of frequencies scanned during a sweep

description: Particle torque due to j cross B force is the volume-integrated Lorentz-force torque exerted on a represented particle distribution by its electric current density interacting with the magnetic field. It is the particle-distribution-resolved parent quantity; species- or population-specific names refine it without implying a toroidal-only projection.
documentation:
Particle torque due to j-cross-B force is the volume-integrated torque exerted on a represented particle distribution by the Lorentz force density generated from that distribution's electric current density and the magnetic field. The physical torque is an axial-vector quantity before any species, population, or coordinate-component qualifier is applied.

The defining volume integral is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_p = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j}_p \times \mathbf{B}\right)\, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ is the particle-distribution-resolved torque, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the torque origin to the volume element, $\mathbf{j}_p$ is the electric current density carried by the represented particle distribution, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $V$ is the integration volume.

This parent does not specify fast, thermal, impurity, neutral, or other particle populations and does not by itself select any coordinate-component projection. Population-specific instances, such as [fast-particle torque due to j-cross-B force](name:fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force), inherit this definition; component-specific quantities are projections of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ rather than redefinitions of the torque source. It excludes torque contributions not arising from the Lorentz force density $\mathbf{j}_p \times \mathbf{B}$ and excludes sums over unrelated plasma sources unless the represented particle distribution is explicitly the aggregation being described.

Sign convention: Positive when a scalar component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ is aligned with the positive direction of the explicitly named projection axis; for a toroidal projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
label_note: int r x (j_p x B) dV for the represented distribution; no registry entry applies; link resolves

description: Coolant pressure at a cooling-circuit inlet is the absolute static pressure of the coolant where it enters a hydraulically defined cooling circuit or component. It is the coolant-specific inlet pressure boundary and excludes gage, dynamic, and stagnation pressure.
documentation:
Coolant pressure at a cooling-circuit inlet is the absolute static thermodynamic pressure of the coolant where it enters a hydraulically defined cooling circuit or component. It denotes the scalar upstream boundary pressure of the coolant and excludes gage pressure, dynamic pressure, and stagnation pressure.

For the same hydraulic flow path, the associated static pressure drop is related to this inlet pressure by:

$$
p_{\mathrm{coolant,in}} = p_{\mathrm{coolant,out}} + \Delta p_{\mathrm{coolant}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{coolant,in}}$ is this inlet absolute static coolant pressure in pascals, $p_{\mathrm{coolant,out}}$ is the corresponding outlet absolute static coolant pressure in pascals, and $\Delta p_{\mathrm{coolant}}$ is the total static pressure drop in pascals, defined positive when the outlet static pressure is lower than the inlet static pressure.

This quantity is the coolant-specific specialization of [pressure at a cooling-circuit inlet]: when the working fluid is coolant, both names denote the same inlet absolute static pressure. It is also the cooling-circuit-inlet value of [coolant pressure](name:coolant_pressure), and it is distinct from pressure loss, pump head, and mechanical stress in the surrounding structure.

dd_sources.documentation: Inlet coolant pressure

label_note: unresolved [pressure at a cooling-circuit inlet]

description: Signed poloidal magnetic-field values forming the linear calibration axis used to characterize a poloidal magnetic-field probe’s nonlinear response.
documentation:
This quantity is the signed poloidal magnetic field assigned to the linear-response reference axis of a poloidal magnetic-field probe. It represents the field value corresponding to the probe signal under an assumed linear field-to-signal relation, rather than the corrected field on a nonlinear response curve.

The linear calibration relation is represented by

$$
S_{\mathrm{lin}} = G B_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{lin}}$ is the probe signal predicted by the linear-response model, $G$ is the linear field-to-signal coefficient, and $B_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the signed calibration-reference magnetic field represented by this quantity.

The quantity applies to the local poloidal magnetic field at the sensing location of the specified poloidal magnetic-field probe. It retains the signed poloidal field rather than a field magnitude, and no summation over probe locations or magnetic-field components is implied. It is an independent calibration-axis quantity, not a plasma-wide or equilibrium-field aggregate.

It is distinct from the local operational field represented by [poloidal magnetic field of a magnetic-field probe](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_of_magnetic_field_probe), which is the probe field value itself, and from the equilibrium reference vector [reference magnetic field](name:reference_magnetic_field). The reference values are paired with the nonlinear-response characterization and do not constitute a single fixed gain or an uncertainty/error quantity. The poloidal component is resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when the signed poloidal field points along the probe's defined positive sensing direction.

dd_sources.documentation: Array of magnetic field values (corresponding to the assumption of a linear relation between magnetic field and probe coil current), for each of which the probe non-linear response is given in ../b_field_non_linear

label_note: the linear-response reference field paired with the non-linear response, as b_field_linear; B as the registry gives; links resolve

description: Full physical extent of a rectangular Motional Stark Effect detector aperture measured along its second local tangential axis.
documentation:
The quantity is the full width of a rectangular Motional Stark Effect detector aperture along the detector's second local tangential axis. It describes the aperture's physical extent, not the coordinate of an individual outline point.

The width is defined by

$$
w_2 = x_{2,\max} - x_{2,\min}
$$

where $w_2$ is the second-local-tangential aperture width, and $x_{2,\max}$ and $x_{2,\min}$ are the maximum and minimum detector-aperture positions along that local axis. The quantity applies only to a rectangular aperture and is a nonnegative full extent.

The second-local-tangential width is the orthogonal aperture dimension paired with the [first-local-tangential detector width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_detector); together, they define the two in-plane dimensions of the rectangular detector aperture. It excludes any aperture position, outline-vertex coordinate, or dimension along the first local tangential axis.

dd_sources.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

label_note: narrows the generic detector width to a Motional Stark Effect detector aperture

description: Flux-surface-averaged field-aligned current density generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive from pressure and density gradients in edge and scrape-off-layer plasma.
documentation:
The quantity is the flux-surface-averaged component of the neoclassically generated bootstrap current density along the magnetic field. It represents the self-generated current associated with pressure and density gradients in edge and scrape-off-layer plasma.

The defining relation is

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{BS}} = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{BS}} \cdot \mathbf{B} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{B_0}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{BS}}$ is the field-aligned bootstrap current density, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{BS}}$ is the bootstrap current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the positive reference magnetic-field magnitude used for the parallel-current normalization.

This quantity includes only the bootstrap-drive contribution and excludes Ohmic, externally driven, and other current mechanisms. The flux-surface average and field-aligned projection distinguish it from the local vector quantity [bootstrap current-density contribution](name:current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive); the linked vector quantity contains directional information that is reduced here to its normalized field-aligned component.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged bootstrap current is aligned with the magnetic field in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

dd_sources.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

label_note: narrows the generic bootstrap parallel current density to edge and scrape-off-layer plasma, where open field lines carry no flux-surface average

description: Dimensionless magnetic flux-expansion factor equal to the upstream poloidal-field magnitude at the outboard midplane separatrix divided by its magnitude at the divertor strike point.
documentation:
Magnetic flux expansion compares the poloidal magnetic-field strength upstream of the divertor with that at the downstream strike point. It quantifies the widening of a magnetic flux tube as it connects the upstream separatrix to the divertor target.

$$
F_x = \frac{B_{p,u}}{B_{p,t}}
$$

where $F_x$ is the magnetic flux-expansion factor, $B_{p,u}$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field at the outboard midplane separatrix, and $B_{p,t}$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field at the strike point.

The quantity is a local ratio for the specified upstream and target locations; it is not summed or averaged over flux surfaces, divertor targets, or strike points. It uses the poloidal-field magnitude rather than the total magnetic-field magnitude or a single cylindrical component. The strike-point location is the geometric point whose major-radius position is described by the [radial coordinate of the strike point](name:radial_coordinate_of_strike_point).

A larger $F_x$ indicates greater magnetic spreading between the upstream separatrix and the target, allowing a given parallel heat flow to be distributed over a wider wetted target area.

dd_sources.documentation: Magnetic flux expansion as defined by Stangeby : ratio between the poloidal field at the midplane separatrix and the poloidal field at the strike-point see formula attached, where u means upstream (midplane separatrix) and t means at divertor target (downstream).

concepts.definition: One quantity divided by another.

symbols.meaning: the quantity before "to" in the name
the quantity after "to" in the name

label_note: F_x = B_p,u/B_p,t as the Stangeby flux expansion in the source and the ratio concept; no template applies; link resolves

description: Signed inclination of the first axis of an oblique parallelogram cross-section of an axisymmetric ferritic element, measured counter-clockwise from the outward radial direction.
documentation:
This quantity is the alpha orientation of the first axis of an oblique, parallelogram-shaped cross-section belonging to a single axisymmetric ferritic element. It specifies the primary orientation of that element in the poloidal plane.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the signed inclination is defined by

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}(\mathbf{a}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}},\, \mathbf{a}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}})
$$

where $\alpha$ is the alpha inclination angle, $\mathbf{a}_1$ is the oriented unit vector along the first axis of the parallelogram cross-section, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the outward radial unit vector, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector, and $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the signed two-argument arctangent.

The quantity applies to one ferritic element and is not an aggregate over multiple elements. It describes the first axis only; it is distinct from the [tilt angle of the ferritic element](name:tilt_angle_of_ferritic_element), which describes the inclination of the second side. Together, the alpha and tilt angles specify the orientations of the two oblique sides of the parallelogram cross-section.

The same alpha-orientation concept is used for other oblique component cross-sections, including an [alpha angle of an iron core segment](name:alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment).

Sign convention: Positive when the first axis tilts from the outward radial direction toward increasing $Z$, counter-clockwise in the poloidal $(R,Z)$ plane.

dd_sources.documentation: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).

label_note: first line never reaches 'angle', against '{qualifier} angle'

description: Faraday rotation of a probing wave’s polarization plane caused by electron density and the magnetic-field component along its plasma path.
documentation:
The Faraday angle is the signed rotation of a probing electromagnetic wave’s polarization plane caused by propagation through magnetized plasma. For an equilibrium state, it is the angle predicted from the electron density and magnetic field encountered along the beam path.

In the cold, weakly dispersive magnetoionic approximation, the plasma-induced rotation is defined by

$$
\theta_F = \frac{e^3\lambda^2}{8\pi^2\epsilon_0 m_e^2 c^3} \int_{\mathcal{L}} n_e(\ell) B_{\parallel}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\theta_F$ is the Faraday rotation angle, $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude, $\lambda$ is the probing-wave vacuum wavelength, $\pi$ is the circle constant, $\epsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $c$ is the speed of light, $\mathcal{L}$ is the segment of the beam path crossing the plasma, $\ell$ is distance along that path, $n_e(\ell)$ is the local electron number density, and $B_{\parallel}(\ell)$ is the signed magnetic-field component along the beam direction.

The quantity applies to the electron contribution accumulated along one probing beam through the plasma. Its aggregation is a line integral along that path, not a local rotation rate, flux-surface average, or sum over multiple beams; optical rotation produced outside the plasma is excluded. The equilibrium-derived value is the rotation predicted by the reconstructed plasma state and is distinct from a directly observed angle or from a residual between prediction and observation.

Faraday angle describes rotation of the polarization plane, whereas [polarization ellipticity of a polarimeter beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam) describes the signed shape of the polarization ellipse through its axis ratio; the two quantities are not interchangeable.

Sign convention: Positive when the polarization plane rotates according to the right-hand rule about the beam propagation direction from its incident reference orientation.

dd_sources.documentation: Measured value
Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium

label_note: bound to constraints/faraday_angle/measured as well as reconstructed, while the text defines the equilibrium-predicted angle and calls it distinct from an observed one; also theta_F where the registry angle symbol is alpha

description: Net energy power leaving the confined plasma through the last closed magnetic flux surface and entering the scrape-off layer.
documentation:
Separatrix power is the net global energy loss from the confined plasma into the scrape-off layer across the last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the aggregate power crossing the entire separatrix rather than a local surface value.

The defining boundary integral is

$$
P_{\rm sep} = \oint_{S_{\rm sep}} \mathbf{S}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix power, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the last closed magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{S}_E$ is the net plasma-energy flux density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the confined plasma toward the scrape-off layer, and $dA$ is an element of separatrix area.

This is a total, net quantity integrated over the complete separatrix. It applies to the confined plasma as a whole, with no selection of species, reaction channel, or individual transport mechanism; outward energy transfer is the plasma loss represented by the quantity. It is not a pointwise energy-flux density or a power associated with a single surface location.

The boundary total is distinct from [radiated power over the core region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), which describes electromagnetic power emitted within the core and is not necessarily equal to power crossing the separatrix. It is also distinct from [power due to conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), which describes conduction-mediated power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces downstream of the separatrix.

dd_sources.documentation: Value

concepts.definition: Last closed flux surface / separatrix. For a flux-surface-averaged quantity apply the flux_surface_averaged operator (DD summary/local/separatrix_average/*); for a bare point value at the outboard midplane use outboard_midplane_separatrix. DD: summary/local/separatrix/*, equilibrium/time_slice/boundary_separatrix.

description: Dimensionless closure parameter that limits the admissible energy-flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
documentation:
This coefficient specifies the strength of the limiter applied to energy transport by neutral particles occupying one selected internal state. It is a closure parameter rather than an energy flux or an energy density.

The limiter imposes the bound

$$
\lvert \mathbf{q}_E \rvert \leq \alpha_E q_{E,\max}
$$

where $\alpha_E$ is this flux-limiter coefficient, $\mathbf{q}_E$ is the energy-flux-density vector carried by the selected neutral internal state, and $q_{E,\max}$ is the prescribed maximum admissible magnitude for that energy flux.

The coefficient applies to the energy channel of neutral transport for the specified internal state. It does not sum over neutral internal states or neutral species, does not represent the energy flux itself, and has no edge-region restriction in its definition. It is distinct from the corresponding momentum limiter, such as the [neutral internal-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region), which constrains momentum rather than energy transport.

The coefficient scales the admissible energy-flux bound in the closure: increasing $\alpha_E$ permits a larger maximum energy flux relative to $q_{E,\max}$, while the coefficient itself remains a dimensionless scalar.

dd_sources.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

label_note: dimensionless bound |q_E| <= alpha_E q_E,max for one neutral state; no template applies; link resolves

description: Upper wavelength of a filter is the vacuum-wavelength coordinate marking the long-wavelength, low-frequency edge of its transmitted spectral band.
documentation:
Upper wavelength of a filter is the spectral coordinate, expressed as vacuum wavelength, that identifies the long-wavelength boundary of a filter's transmitted spectral band. It is a property of the filter transmission response, rather than the rest-frame wavelength of a spectral line or the wavelength inside a material medium.

For the upper boundary associated with the lower temporal frequency, the vacuum wavelength is defined by:

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{upper}} = \frac{c}{\nu_{\mathrm{low}}}
$$

where $\lambda_{\mathrm{upper}}$ is the upper boundary vacuum wavelength, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, and $\nu_{\mathrm{low}}$ is the lower temporal frequency corresponding to that boundary.

This quantity applies specifically to the long-wavelength boundary of the transmitted passband and is not a band-average or a full transmission function. It complements the [lower wavelength of a filter](name:lower_wavelength_of_filter), which marks the short-wavelength boundary; together, the two boundaries determine the [width of a filter]. The parent [wavelength of a filter](name:wavelength_of_filter) also includes nominal characteristic wavelengths such as a reference wavelength.

dd_sources.documentation: Upper bound of the filter wavelength range
Upper bound of the filter wavelength range

label_note: unresolved [width of a filter]; otherwise the long-wavelength passband edge with a '{zone} wavelength {locus}' opening and lambda as the registry gives

description: Toroidal angle of a coil-conductor element is the azimuthal coordinate φ of a specified geometric locus on the element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, with R the major radius and Z the vertical height. It covers start points, centers, intermediate points, and end points.
documentation:
Toroidal angle of a coil-conductor element is the azimuthal coordinate $\phi$ of a specified geometric locus on a conductor element about the toroidal symmetry axis. It is the angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\phi=0$ is the chosen radial half-plane.

For the same locus represented in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and $+\hat{x}$ lying in the $\phi=0$ half-plane, the principal angular representative is defined by

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y, x)
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the locus along $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the quadrant-resolving angle from $+\hat{x}$ to the horizontal projection of the locus.

The scope is locus-general within the coil-conductor-element geometry: start point, center, intermediate point, and end point angles use the same coordinate definition when that locus is selected. The aggregation convention is pointwise; the value belongs to one geometric point of one conductor element and is not an average over an element, a coil, or a periodic sector.

This absolute cylindrical coordinate is distinct from the element's major radius $R$ and vertical height $Z$, and from any local orientation or twist angle of a conductor cross-section. Together with $R$ and $Z$ for the same locus, $\phi$ specifies the cylindrical position of that point; angular values that differ by an integer multiple of $2\pi$ represent the same radial half-line.

Sign convention: Positive when the radial direction from the toroidal symmetry axis to the conductor-element locus is rotated from the $\phi=0$ half-plane toward increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

dd_sources.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

concepts.definition: The azimuthal angle about the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.

symbols.meaning: toroidal angle

label_note: phi = atan2(y,x) for a selected element locus, covering both the centre and end-point sources; opens 'Toroidal angle of'; phi as the registry gives

description: Fast-particle torque due to the j×B force is the volume-integrated torque vector acting on the fast-particle population through the magnetic Lorentz force density generated by its current density and the magnetic field.
documentation:
Fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force is the volume-integrated torque vector acting on the fast-particle population through the magnetic part of the Lorentz force density associated with the fast-particle current density and the magnetic field. It represents angular-momentum transfer to that fast-particle population, not to thermal particles or material structures.

The torque vector over a volume $V$ is defined by the moment of the $j \times B$ force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j}_f \times \mathbf{B}\right)\, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B}$ is the fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the chosen torque origin to the volume element, $\mathbf{j}_f$ is the fast-particle current density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This vector parent is distinguished from component-specific projections; [toroidal fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force) is the toroidal component of the same fast-particle torque. It excludes torque channels not represented by the fast-particle current-cross-magnetic-field force density.

Sign convention: Positive when a reported component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its stated projection axis, with vector cross products evaluated by the right-hand rule; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is positive along $+\hat{\phi}$ toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side.
label_note: int r x (j_f x B) dV for the fast population; no registry entry applies; link resolves

description: Diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive radial ion momentum flux to the local radial ion momentum gradient, expressing down-gradient redistribution within the total ion population summed over charge states.
documentation:
The radial ion momentum diffusivity $D_{[3m\mathrm{rad}}^i$ is the effective diffusion coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the radial component of momentum across magnetic flux surfaces within the total ion population summed over all charge states. It is the radial component of the broader [ion momentum diffusivity].

The flux-surface-integrated diffusive radial ion momentum flux is represented by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{mom},i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -V'\mathcal{M}_iD_{\mathrm{rad}}^i\left\langle \left|\nabla\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\right|^2 \right\rangle \frac{d v_{r,i}}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{mom},i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of radial ion momentum through a flux surface, $V'$ is the derivative of enclosed volume with respect to the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, $\mathcal{M}_i$ is the total ion mass density, $v_{r,i}$ is the radial component of the mean ion fluid velocity, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and angle brackets denote a flux-surface average.

The coefficient applies to the total ion population, with contributions summed over ion species and all charge states. Here radial denotes the flux-surface transport direction associated with increasing $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, not a cylindrical-$R$ projection; parallel and poloidal momentum channels are distinct quantities. Unlike [ion-state momentum diffusivity], this quantity is not resolved by charge state.

Replacing the radial momentum component with the poloidal component gives the corresponding [poloidal ion momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity); both are directional components of [ion momentum diffusivity], while the minus sign expresses down-gradient diffusive transport.

description: Cumulative post-breakdown oxygen inventory delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with eight count units per neutral oxygen atom.
documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of oxygen atoms admitted after plasma breakdown through gas injection, converted to an equivalent-electron count. Each oxygen atom contributes eight equivalent electrons, corresponding to oxygen's atomic number.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 8N_{\mathrm{O}}(t) = 8\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the cumulative oxygen-atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen-atom injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The count quantities are dimensionless and the injection rate has units of inverse seconds.

Only oxygen delivered after plasma breakdown by gas injection is included; prefill oxygen is excluded and is represented by accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection. The instantaneous counterpart is [oxygen_source_rate](name:oxygen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), while accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection uses the corresponding atomic-number weighting for carbon.

description: Rate coefficient multiplying the primary ion momentum quantity to represent its implicit source or sink contribution in transport equations.
documentation:
This quantity is the coefficient for the implicit contribution to an ion momentum source term. It represents proportional momentum addition or removal associated with the primary ion momentum quantity, without selecting a particular directional component.

The implicit source contribution is defined by

$$
S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} = C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} M_i
$$

where $S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit ion momentum source contribution, $C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this rate coefficient, and $M_i$ is the primary ion momentum quantity to which the coefficient is applied.

The quantity applies to ion momentum and is independent of the component or direction selected by a specialization. It describes the coefficient itself, not the resulting momentum source and not the primary momentum quantity. A positive coefficient represents proportional momentum sourcing, whereas a negative coefficient represents proportional momentum removal.

It is the implicit, proportional component of the broader [ion momentum source rate](name:ion_momentum_source_rate). The [toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate](name:toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is a directional specialization in which the same coefficient concept is applied to the toroidal ion momentum quantity.

description: Full transverse diameter of a circular diagnostic aperture, measured across its center between opposite points on the circumferential boundary.
documentation:
This quantity is the full transverse extent of the clear circular opening at the diagnostic entrance pupil, measured between opposite points on its circumferential boundary.

The diameter is defined by

$$
D = 2r
$$

where $D$ is the aperture diameter and $r$ is the geometric radius given by the [radius of the diagnostic aperture](name:radius_of_diagnostic_aperture).

The quantity describes the opening geometry only; it excludes aperture thickness, housing dimensions, and the width of a noncircular aperture. The diameter determines the geometric area and contributes to the solid-angle acceptance together with the aperture-to-source distance.

description: Dimensionless real oscillation frequency of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized by the positive reference angular frequency for the same perpendicular wavevector.
documentation:
The quantity is the real oscillation-frequency component of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the local flux-tube approximation. It is evaluated for a specified wavevector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field.

The normalized frequency is defined by

$$
\omega_{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\omega)}{\omega_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\omega$ is the complex eigenfrequency and $\omega_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference angular frequency used for the same eigenvalue problem.

Together with the [normalized linear growth rate](name:linear_growth_rate_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), this quantity specifies the real and imaginary components of the normalized complex eigenfrequency. Its sign follows the temporal Fourier and wave-propagation convention used to define $\omega$.

dd_sources.documentation: Frequency

description: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to all plasma particle populations and integrated over all spatial locations.
documentation:
Total absorbed wave power is the total rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to all plasma particle populations, with contributions integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the combined energy of all included plasma particle populations, $t$ is time, and the subscript “waves” restricts the derivative to direct energy transfer from the coherent electromagnetic-wave field.

This quantity is globally aggregated: it is summed over all species, charge states, populations, and spatial locations. It includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes electromagnetic power that remains in the wave field and energy subsequently redistributed between particle populations by collisions.

It is the species-summed specialization of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), unlike [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), which is restricted to electron populations. It is also the global counterpart of [total absorbed wave power at the inside flux surface](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface), which retains only the power enclosed within a selected flux surface; Fourier-resolved contributions are represented by [per-toroidal-mode total absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power).

dd_sources.documentation: Total absorbed wave power

label_note: species-summed direct wave-to-particle power over the plasma volume; opening fits '{modifiers} power {locus}'; P as the registry gives; links resolve

description: Non-negative geometric separation between the inner and outer material interfaces of a breeder blanket layer along the specified thickness direction.
documentation:
Non-negative geometric separation between the inner and outer material interfaces of a breeder blanket layer is the local through-thickness of that layer along the specified thickness direction. The quantity applies to a single material or functional layer within the blanket, not to the total breeder blanket module build.

The layer thickness is defined by the separation of the two bounding interfaces along the thickness coordinate:

$$
d_\ell = \left|s_{\ell,\mathrm{out}} - s_{\ell,\mathrm{in}}\right|
$$

where $d_\ell$ is the layer thickness in m, and $s_{\ell,\mathrm{in}}$ and $s_{\ell,\mathrm{out}}$ are the signed coordinates in m of the inner and outer layer interfaces along the specified thickness direction.

It is not the toroidal width, poloidal height, surface extent, or volume-equivalent thickness of the layer. It is distinct from module-level quantities such as thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module, [lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module), and [upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module). For a radially stacked layer, the thickness direction is the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

dd_sources.documentation: Thickness of this layer evaluated at the midplane

description: Photon-count radiance from an identified emission transition, integrated over its spectral line interval and resolved by projected area and viewing solid angle.
documentation:
Photon-count line radiance is the photon emission rate from one identified transition accumulated along the emitting line of sight, resolved by projected collecting area and viewing solid angle.

The defining photon-count radiance is

$$
L_{\gamma,\ell} = \frac{d^3 N_{\gamma,\ell}}{dt\,dA_{\perp}\,d\Omega}
$$

where $L_{\gamma,\ell}$ is the line radiance, $N_{\gamma,\ell}$ is the number of photons from transition $\ell$, $\ell$ identifies the emission transition, $t$ is time, $A_{\perp}$ is collecting area projected normal to the viewing direction, and $\Omega$ is viewing solid angle.

The quantity applies to one identified emission transition without imposing a particular emitting species, charge state, or line-splitting mechanism. Photon counts are integrated across the selected spectral-line interval and accumulated along the viewing path; the result is not resolved per wavelength.

Integrating [photon-number spectral radiance] over wavelength across the selected line interval gives this line radiance under matching projected-area and solid-angle conventions. The qualified [motional-Stark photon radiance at a spectral line] is a specialized instance restricted to an identified motional-Stark-split component. Unlike energy radiance, this quantity counts photons without weighting them by photon energy; conversion to energy radiance requires applying that energy weighting before integration.

description: Effective collection area of a Langmuir probe, obtained by projecting its plasma-facing collector surface onto the plane normal to the local magnetic field.
documentation:
The effective area of a Langmuir probe is the plasma-facing collector surface area projected onto the plane perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction. It represents the area governing particle collection when the sheath is magnetized.

$$
A_{\mathrm{eff}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{w}}} \left|\hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}\right|\,dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective collection area, $S_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the plasma-exposed collector surface, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the local outward unit normal, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local magnetic-field unit vector, and $dA$ is an element of collector surface area. The absolute dot product gives the geometrical projection factor.

Unlike the total [area of a Langmuir probe], this quantity accounts for magnetic-field orientation; unlike the [wetted area of a Langmuir probe](name:wetted_area_of_langmuir_probe), it is not the unprojected plasma-exposed surface area.

dd_sources.documentation: Effective collection area of the probe surface, varying with time due to e.g. changes in the magnetic field line incidence angle

description: Z component in the right-handed Cartesian (x̂, ŷ, ẑ) basis of the unit direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the neutron detector center, with ẑ vertical. It is the vertical direction cosine, not a position coordinate.
documentation:
Z component in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis of the unit direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the neutron detector center is the projection of that voxel-to-detector direction onto the vertical basis vector $\hat{z}$. It represents the vertical direction cosine of the ray from the voxel toward the detector center.

The component is defined by the normalized displacement from the voxel position to the detector-center position:

$$
u_z = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v) \cdot \hat{z}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v \rVert}
$$

where $u_z$ is the z component of the direction unit vector, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the field-of-view voxel position, $\mathbf{r}_d$ is the neutron detector-center position, and $\hat{z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

Together with [x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector) and [y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector), it forms the direction-cosine triplet of the same voxel-to-detector ray, so $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ and $-1 \le u_z \le 1$. This quantity is a direction cosine, not a vertical position coordinate or displacement magnitude; it is the neutron-detector analog of [z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).

dd_sources.documentation: Component along Z axis  for each voxel

description: Signed safety-factor value on the closed magnetic flux surface where the magnitude of field-line winding is smallest, distinct from that surface’s location.
documentation:
The minimum safety factor is the signed field-line winding number evaluated on the nested closed magnetic flux surface where the magnitude of the safety factor is smallest. It represents the extremal value of the safety-factor function within the confined closed-surface domain.

The minimizing value is defined by

$$
q_{\min} = q(\rho_\ast), \qquad \rho_\ast \in \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0 \leq \rho \leq 1} |q(\rho)|
$$

where $q(\rho)$ is the signed [safety factor](name:safety_factor) on the flux surface labeled by $\rho$, $\rho_\ast$ is the label of a surface at which the magnitude $|q(\rho)|$ is minimized, and $q_{\min}$ is the signed value evaluated there. The label $\rho$ is a monotonic flux-surface coordinate whose endpoints denote the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface. In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The extremum is taken over all nested closed magnetic flux surfaces and is neither a flux-surface average nor a sum. The location-defining quantity is separate: [poloidal magnetic flux at minimum safety factor] identifies the corresponding surface, while this quantity reports only the signed safety factor. It is also distinct from a safety factor evaluated at a prescribed locus, such as the magnetic axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angle advance of a magnetic field line is in the direction of increasing $\phi$ as the poloidal angle $\theta$ increases.
